chunks: And through his chain of narration, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)

He said: Whoever comes to you intending to cause disunity among the community, and oppressively seize the affairs of the nation, and take authority without consultation, kill him, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has granted permission for that.

key_terms.الْأُمَّة: The nation or people, often used interchangeably with community in political contexts
key_terms.الْجَمَاعَة: The community or congregation, referring to the unified body of Muslims
key_terms.مَشُورَة: Consultation, a key principle in Islamic governance and leadership

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing someone who usurps authority and causes disunity in the community?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* underscores the principle of *al-walaa'* and the preservation of communal unity (*jamaa*) by authorizing the removal of a usurper (*ghasib*) who seizes authority without legitimate consultation (*mashura*). In Shia scholarly tradition, this serves as a foundational justification for political resistance against illegitimate rule, linking the Prophet’s direct command to divine permission (*idhn*) for maintaining the integrity of the Ummah.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-254 According to the same documentation, it is narrated that the Prophet (S) said,

“Whenever someone comes and tries to make disunion in the society and oppressively takes over the affairs of the society, you should kill him. Indeed the Honorable the Exalted God has granted this permission.”
